learningObjectives.title: The break with Rome and the Reformation

questions.q: In which year did Henry VIII become King of England?
questions.explain: Henry VIII succeeded his father Henry VII in 1509.

questions.q: Which senior office, giving him control of the legal system, did Thomas Wolsey hold from 1515?
options: Lord Chancellor
Principal Secretary
Lord Protector
Archbishop of Canterbury
questions.explain: Wolsey became Lord Chancellor in 1515, the leading government and legal post.

questions.q: What name was given to the lavish 1520 meeting between Henry VIII and King Francis I of France?
options: The Field of Cloth of Gold
The Amicable Grant
The Treaty of London
The Pilgrimage of Grace
questions.explain: The Field of Cloth of Gold in 1520 was a spectacular display of wealth arranged by Wolsey.

questions.q: Which 1534 Act made Henry VIII 'Supreme Head of the Church of England'?
options: The Act of Supremacy
The Act in Restraint of Appeals
The Treasons Act
The Act of Succession
questions.explain: The 1534 Act of Supremacy declared Henry, not the Pope, head of the English Church.

questions.q: Who became Archbishop of Canterbury in 1533 and declared Henry's marriage to Catherine of Aragon void?
options: Thomas Cranmer
Thomas More
Reginald Pole
John Fisher
questions.explain: Thomas Cranmer, made Archbishop in 1533, annulled Henry's first marriage, allowing marriage to Anne Boleyn.

questions.q: Which former Lord Chancellor was executed in 1535 for refusing to accept Henry as head of the Church?
options: Sir Thomas More
Thomas Cromwell
Robert Aske
Thomas Wolsey
questions.explain: Sir Thomas More was executed in 1535 for refusing to swear the oath accepting the royal supremacy.

questions.q: What was the name of Cromwell's 1535 survey valuing the wealth of the Church and monasteries?
options: The Valor Ecclesiasticus
The Domesday Book
The Eltham Ordinances
The Act of Union
questions.explain: The Valor Ecclesiasticus of 1535 assessed Church wealth ahead of the dissolution of the monasteries.

questions.q: In which year did an Act begin the dissolution of the smaller monasteries?
questions.explain: The 1536 Act for the Suppression of Lesser Monasteries began the dissolution, with larger houses following by 1540.

questions.q: Why did Wolsey's 1525 Amicable Grant fail?
options: It was a non-parliamentary tax that provoked widespread resistance and was abandoned
It was rejected by the Pope in Rome
It was blocked by the House of Lords
It sparked a rebellion led by Robert Aske
questions.explain: The Amicable Grant, a forced tax to fund war with France, met such opposition that Henry cancelled it, damaging Wolsey.

questions.q: What was the main reason for Wolsey's fall from power in 1529?
options: He failed to secure the annulment of Henry's marriage to Catherine of Aragon
He led a rebellion against the King
He converted to Protestantism
He refused to become a Cardinal
questions.explain: Unable to obtain the Pope's agreement to end the marriage, Wolsey lost Henry's favour and was stripped of office.

questions.q: What was the main purpose of the Court of Star Chamber under Wolsey?
options: To deliver fair justice, including to the poor, and curb powerful nobles
To collect taxes for war with France
To try heretics and Protestants
To manage Henry's royal household
questions.explain: Wolsey used Star Chamber to enforce justice impartially and check over-mighty subjects.

questions.q: Why did Pope Clement VII refuse to annul Henry's marriage to Catherine of Aragon?
options: Catherine was the aunt of Charles V, whose troops controlled Rome and the Pope
Henry had already remarried without permission
England had already left the Catholic Church
Catherine had produced a healthy male heir
questions.explain: Charles V, Catherine's nephew, dominated Rome after 1527, so the Pope dared not rule against her.

questions.q: What did the 1533 Act in Restraint of Appeals achieve?
options: It banned appeals to the Pope in Rome, keeping legal cases within England
It dissolved all the monasteries
It made Cromwell chief minister
It reunited England with Rome
questions.explain: The Act stopped appeals to Rome, allowing Cranmer to settle the annulment in England.

questions.q: What mainly motivated the 1536 Pilgrimage of Grace led by Robert Aske?
options: Opposition to religious changes and the dissolution of the monasteries
A demand to make Henry Supreme Head of the Church
Support for Wolsey's return to power
A tax revolt against the Field of Cloth of Gold
questions.explain: The northern rising protested against the Reformation and the closure of monasteries.

questions.q: Why did Thomas Cromwell fall from power and face execution in 1540?
options: He arranged Henry's unpopular marriage to Anne of Cleves, giving his enemies their chance
He refused the oath of supremacy
He led the Pilgrimage of Grace
He secretly restored the monasteries
questions.explain: Henry's dislike of Anne of Cleves let Cromwell's rivals bring him down; he was executed in July 1540.

questions.q: What was a main aim of Wolsey's Eltham Ordinances of 1526?
options: To reform the royal household and reduce the number of gentlemen in the Privy Chamber
To raise a new tax for war with France
To close the smaller monasteries
To arrange Henry's annulment
questions.explain: The Eltham Ordinances cut household costs and reduced the Privy Chamber, also removing potential rivals to Wolsey.

questions.q: A student argues that Wolsey dominated both Church and state in the 1510s and 1520s. Which fact best supports this claim?
options: He simultaneously held the offices of Lord Chancellor, Cardinal and papal legate
He led the Pilgrimage of Grace against Henry
He wrote the Act of Supremacy
He arranged the marriage to Anne of Cleves
questions.explain: Holding the top state office plus the highest Church roles gave Wolsey unrivalled power under Henry.

questions.q: A historian argues Henry's desire for a male heir drove the break with Rome. Which evidence best supports this interpretation?
options: Henry sought to annul his marriage to Catherine of Aragon, who had not produced a surviving son
Henry met Francis I at the Field of Cloth of Gold
Wolsey introduced the Amicable Grant
Cromwell surveyed Church wealth in 1535
questions.explain: Henry's push to end his first marriage to gain a legitimate son triggered the split from Rome.

questions.q: A student wants to show Cromwell strengthened the Crown's finances. Which action provides the strongest evidence?
options: The dissolution of the monasteries transferred their wealth and lands to the Crown
The signing of the Field of Cloth of Gold treaty
The failure of the Amicable Grant
The Eltham Ordinances reforming the household
questions.explain: Closing the monasteries channelled vast monastic wealth to Henry, greatly boosting royal income.

questions.q: John Fisher, Bishop of Rochester, was executed in 1535. A student uses this to show there was resistance to the royal supremacy. Which statement best explains why?
options: He refused to accept Henry as Supreme Head of the Church and was executed for treason
He led a tax revolt against Wolsey
He arranged Henry's marriage to Anne of Cleves
He supported the dissolution of the monasteries
questions.explain: Like Thomas More, Fisher would not swear the oath of supremacy and was executed, showing opposition to the changes.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel GCSE History (1HI0) specification; Henry VIII & His Ministers 1509-40
